page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: A black body is a body that absorbs
completely all the radiation falling on it,
and on heating emits radiation of all
steps.why: The definition has two halves, absorption and emission, and the examiner looks for both. A perfect absorber must also be a perfect emitter, otherwise the body would keep heating up without limit.
common_mistakes: Writing only the absorption half and stopping there.
Saying a black body looks black. It is defined by what it absorbs and emits, not by its colour.
steps.memory_tip: Two halves in one line: absorbs everything, emits everything.
steps.margin_note: One sentence carries this mark. Do not write a paragraph.

steps.label: How it is realised

lines.text: Radiation emitted by it is black body radiation

lines: No perfect black body exists in nature.
A hollow sphere coated inside with lamp
black, with a small hole, acts as one.
steps.why: Radiation entering the small hole is reflected again and again inside and cannot come out, so the hole absorbs everything. This is why the hollow sphere is the standard laboratory model of a black body.
common_mistakes: Naming a black-coloured object as a perfect black body. No real surface absorbs every wavelength.
steps.memory_tip: Picture the small hole in a hollow sphere. Radiation goes in and never comes back out.
steps.margin_note: Naming the hollow sphere with a small hole is what earns this second mark.

insider_note: A three-star question that is asked in one line. Write the absorb half and the emit half as one sentence, then name the hollow sphere. Nothing more is needed at 2 marks.
